text:
Alex: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection change we are seeing a big drop in KV/prefix cache hit-rate for chat workloads on hosted. Example: route /v1/chat/streaming: hit-rate went from ~2.1% -> 0.4%. Affects 3 of 4 high-volume routes. Posting profiler excerpts below and a quick hypothesis. Anyone on this?

Cheng: Can you paste the raw numbers and the commit? which clusters/regions?

Alex: Sure. Short snippets: 
```
route: /v1/chat/streaming
pre-deploy (2025-11-01): prefix_cache_hits=2100, prefix_cache_lookups=100k, hit_rate=0.021
post-deploy (2025-11-04): prefix_cache_hits=160, prefix_cache_lookups=40k, hit_rate=0.004
KV cache size and evictions ~unchanged.
profiling: more kernel switching on short seqs; continuous-batching spike + slightly different chunk boundaries.
```
We also see increase in average latency for cold paths by ~12ms. Commit is 7a8c9f4 (kernel auto selector heuristics).

Maria: Hmm. My gut is that cache keying includes chunk boundaries or kernel-id fingerprint. If the kernel selection changed chunking/seq grouping, the canonicalized prefix may differ so lookups miss. Did the change alter how we compute prefix_key? (like including tokenization offsets)

Cheng: Good call. The selector did start splitting some 1-16 token requests differently to favor a smaller-kernel path. That can change the boundary where we cut the prefix for the key. Also we recently added a kernel_version tag to the model variant keying for routing experiments — could be leaking into cache key.

Priya: Also worth checking SDK/client behavior: streaming clients commonly set the cache header differently (we defaulted the JS SDK to opt-in:false for streaming to avoid delivering partial cached responses). Any change to streaming behavior/headers could flip many requests to non-cacheable.

Alex: Repro steps I used: run 10k synthetic chat messages (short prompts, repeated prefixes) against hosted region-us-east-1, streaming=true. Compare with streaming=false. Notes: streaming=false hit_rate ~2.0% post-deploy; streaming=true hit_rate ~0.6%. So streaming path seems hurt more.

Cheng: Action items: 1) Triage whether cache key includes kernel_version/kernel_selector hash. 2) Add metric labels for cache_key_version and kernel_variant so we can correlate. 3) Quick rollback candidate: revert kernel auto-splitting in selector.

infra-bot: deploy 7a8c9f4 rolled out to us-east-1 at 2025-11-04T03:12:10Z (sha:7a8c9f4) :arrow_down_small:

Maria: Quick mitigation idea — canonicalize the prefix key to strip any kernel-specific metadata and normalize whitespace/token offsets. Also add a short warmup prefetch on model pin/load that primes KV cache for common prefixes (preheat endpoint).

Priya: From SDK side I can add an explicit opt-in header and a flag: `cacheMode: 'strict'|'auto'|'opt-in'`. For streaming: we should allow `cacheMode: 'opt-in'` and only commit to cache at stream EOF (or after final chunk) so partial streaming doesn't create partial keys. Will push a PR for JS + Python SDKs. Example curl header we should support: `-H "x-redwood-cache: opt-in;commit_on_eof=true"`

Cheng: Can you also provide a curl + prefetch example so infra can try hotfix warmup?

Alex: Prefetch endpoint example (works on dedicated/hosted):
```
# preheat common prefixes for model: gpt-redwood-3
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models/gpt-redwood-3/prefetch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prefixes": ["Summarize:", "Rewrite:", "Translate to French:"], "concurrency": 4}'
```
This primes KV caches and improved hit-rate in a quick smoke test from 0.4%->1.2% on the affected route. Not full recovery but helps.

Maria: Good. Also we should add a short lived experiment to backfill cache key mapping from old->new (when we detect old key patterns, insert a copy under new canonicalized key) to prevent long tail cache misses after we change key scheme.

Priya: SDK changes: I'll default new SDKs to `cacheMode: 'opt-in'` but add telemetry to see client adoption. Also I'll update quickstart with header example and a note about streaming edge case. Will add tests to ensure streaming+commit_on_eof true actually writes only after final chunk.

Cheng: For immediate rollback: ops, can we revert 7a8c9f4 in us-east-1 and run the synthetic workload? If rollback is heavy, we can also patch cache-key canonicalization in runtime which should be lighter. Thoughts?

Alex: Patch is probably faster and safer. I can prototype the canonicalization: remove kernel_version tag, normalize token offsets to nearest lower multiple of 8, and strip trailing whitespace. I'll push a small runtime flag `runtime.kv.canonicalize_prefix_keys=true` behind a config so ops can toggle.

infra-bot: Incident ticket created: INT-2025-1891; assigned to @Cheng and @Alex. Monitoring alert set: prefix_cache_hit_rate < 0.5% sustained 30m on any prod route. :eyes:

Cheng: I'll pair with Alex on the patch. Also will add a gauge `prefix_key_version` so dashboards show old vs new keys. Maria please add alert runbook steps for backfill mapping.

Maria: Will do. Also recommend adding a perf regression test to eng-releases pipeline that runs a small synthetic prefix-heavy workload and asserts hit_rate delta < 0.5% compared to baseline.

Alex: Thanks — I'll start the canonicalize PR and run a smoke with prefetch. Priya LMK when SDK flag PR is up so we can coordinate releasing together. :thumbsup:

Priya: Will ping when PR is ready. Will also add doc snippet for `x-redwood-cache` header and streaming note.

Cheng: Plan: patch canonicalization -> smoke prefetch -> if green, keep change; if not, rollback selector. Update here as we test.

Alex: Updating thread with results after smoke tests.
